ai.title: Tweak agentContext TTL and reorder tool results in main-prompt
ai.summary: Reordered tool results to appear before agent step instructions in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Added `timeToLive: 'userPrompt'` to the agent context block. This adjusts message expiration logic and prompt structure.

eli5.text: The assistant's short-term memory now clears out a bit differently, and the order of some behind-the-scenes notes it looks at has been shuffled. When the assistant starts a new round of work, tool results (like search answers or data it just fetched) now appear earlier in its thinking stack than they did before, right after old chat, and before a block of special instructions. The agent context, which holds briefing info, now tells the system to forget it after the current prompt finishes, instead of holding on a bit longer. This is live today and affects how the assistant processes each step internally; you would not see a visible change unless you were inspecting its internal flow. No features are added or removed - only the arrangement and timing of internal prompts.

ai.title: Refactor backend tools.ts for modularity
ai.summary: Refactored `backend/src/tools.ts` to separate tool definitions from implementation details, enhancing modularity. Updated `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to use `Extract` utility type for stricter type checking on `ToolCall` parameters. This change improves code maintainability and type safety within the backend services.

eli5.text: The team reorganized how the assistant handles tool instructions, moving the detailed tool definitions into their own clearly separated section so they can be managed independently. While doing this, they also tightened the type safety around how tool calls are validated, reducing the chance of mismatches between what the assistant sends and what the tools expect. If you were looking at the code, you'd see tool schemas are now more cleanly isolated and the callback logic uses stricter typing; from a functional standpoint, this is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that makes the backend easier to maintain and less prone to type-related bugs.

ai.title: calculate-monthly-usage.ts defaults to current month
ai.summary: calculate-monthly-usage.ts defaults to current month. Static '2025-04' fallback replaced with dynamic Date parsing. Internal tooling script only. Month extracted via toISOString().split('-') concatenation.

eli5.text: When someone runs the monthly usage report script without specifying a month, it now automatically uses whichever month you actually happen to be running it instead of always falling back to a fixed month from earlier this year. The tool is an internal script only, so ordinary users won't notice anything. If you look at the script's source, you'll see that the hard-coded month has been swapped out for a small routine that pulls the current date and reads the year-month out of it. The change is live today the moment the updated script is used on a machine.

ai.title: Add ftfilepicker008 and ftfilepickertopk002 tuning configs
ai.summary: Adds two new fine-tuning configurations to the file selection tooling: `ft_filepicker_008` (expanded data/epochs from 007) and `ft_filepicker_topk_002` (early-stop dash suffix experiment). `collect-tuning-data.ts` introduces an `ADD_DASHES_TO_TOP_FEW_DATA` flag that appends three lines of dashes to training targets and updates prompt instructions to enforce this stop pattern. The default trace sampling limit in the main script was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000 to support the smaller `topk_002` validation run.

eli5.text: Two new training recipes for the file-picking assistant are now set up and ready as of May 31, 2025. One builds on the previous recipe with more practice data and longer study time, while the other teaches the assistant to stop its answer early by ending with three lines of dashes, and it is tested on a smaller, focused set of examples. Because that second recipe expects fewer examples, the system now gathers up to 1,000 examples for validation instead of 10,000. You won't see the new recipes appear anywhere yet, they are configured but not launched.

ai.title: Remove deprecated flags and simplify npm README
ai.summary: Removed obsolete `--lite` and `--max` cost/quality tradeoff flags from `npm-app/README.md`. Simplified troubleshooting section by replacing detailed nvm installation instructions with a generic Node reinstallation recommendation. Added `/help` command to Tips section to improve discoverability of available commands.

eli5.text: You no longer need to worry about picking between cheaper or higher-quality responses when talking to the assistant it just works the way it works. If you hit installation problems, instead of following detailed steps to switch Node versions yourself, you're now pointed to simply reinstall Node from its official site. The help section now tells you to type a slash or /help to see what commands you can use, so those tips are easier to find.
